items.stem: Why does money remove the problem of double coincidence of wants?
items.answer: (1) Money acts as an intermediate in the exchange process. (2) A person can sell goods for money and use that money to buy what he or she wants.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: (1) Money acts as an intermediate in the exchange process. (2) A person can sell goods for money and use that money to buy what he or she wants.

items.stem: Why are demand deposits considered money?
items.answer: (1) They can be withdrawn on demand and used for payments. (2) Cheques against them are widely accepted as a means of payment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: (1) They can be withdrawn on demand and used for payments. (2) Cheques against them are widely accepted as a means of payment.

items.stem: Describe three modern forms of money.
items.answer: (1) Currency – paper notes and coins issued by the RBI. (2) Deposits with banks that can be withdrawn on demand. (3) Payments by cheque and digital modes from bank accounts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any three points: (1) Currency – paper notes and coins issued by the RBI. (2) Deposits with banks that can be withdrawn on demand. (3) Payments by cheque and digital modes from bank accounts.

items.stem:
(a) Explain the problems of the barter system and how money solves them. (3 marks)
(b) Why are demand deposits considered money? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Barter needs double coincidence of wants. (2) Goods are hard to divide and store. (3) There is no common measure of value. (4) Money is a medium of exchange, a measure of value and a store of value. (b) (1) They can be withdrawn on demand and used for payments. (2) Cheques against them are widely accepted as a means of payment.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) Barter needs double coincidence of wants. (2) Goods are hard to divide and store. (3) There is no common measure of value. (4) Money is a medium of exchange, a measure of value and a store of value. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) They can be withdrawn on demand and used for payments. (2) Cheques against them are widely accepted as a means of payment.

items.stem:
(a) Explain how Self-Help Groups help solve the problem of lack of collateral for the poor. (3 marks)
(b) Why do Self-Help Groups help the poor get credit? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) The group takes responsibility for repaying loans. (2) Peer pressure ensures repayment. (3) Banks lend to the group without collateral. (4) Members get timely loans at reasonable interest, freeing them from moneylenders. (b) (1) The group as a whole is responsible for repayment, so no collateral is needed. (2) Banks are willing to lend to the group after it has saved regularly for a year or two.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) The group takes responsibility for repaying loans. (2) Peer pressure ensures repayment. (3) Banks lend to the group without collateral. (4) Members get timely loans at reasonable interest, freeing them from moneylenders. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) The group as a whole is responsible for repayment, so no collateral is needed. (2) Banks are willing to lend to the group after it has saved regularly for a year or two.
